params.name: kmax
params.let: 5 if b == 2 else (4 if b == 3 else 3)

params.why: keeps the constant term q to at most three digits

stem: Calculate the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y={=a}\cdot {=b}^{x}{=signed(q)}$. Write your answer as a point $(x, y)$.
solution: The $x$-intercept is where the graph cuts the $x$-axis, so we let $y=0$.
Move the constant term to the other side: ${=m}={=a}\cdot {=b}^{x}$.
Divide both sides by ${=a}$ to leave the power on its own: ${=n}={=b}^{x}$.
The bases are the same, so the exponents are equal: $x={=k}$.
notes: Standard: the book's own typical x-intercept exercise in its clean form, as ex6-5-4b (y = 1/4.4^x - 1, so 4 = 4^x and x = 1). q is built as -a.b^k so that, after isolating the power, the right-hand side is exactly a power of b and x = k is a whole number; no trial and error or rounding. a is never 1 or -1 (so '1\cdot' is never printed) and may be negative, in which case q is positive. kmax keeps b^k at most 32 (b=2), 81 (b=3) or 64 and 125 (b=4, 5); |a.b^k| is capped at 400.
